entries.title: Author lists start folded at the top
entries.body: The run of authors, affiliations and contact details under an article's title starts folded away, so you begin at the article itself; 'Show authors and details' at the top opens it, as does jumping to one of those lines. The folding is cautious and will not catch every author list. The title is no longer shown twice, and the back arrow at the top is gone: the Spideryarn mark in the bottom bar takes you to your library. Authors' names are also picked up from more arXiv web pages.

entries.title: Five modes move into a More menu
entries.body: Quotes, Glossary, FAQ, Ideas and Timeline, where available, sit in a More menu in the bottom bar; the mode you have open keeps its own button. On a short screen, such as a phone held sideways, the menu scrolls. On first opening an article, the bar fades in after a second, unless your device is set to reduce motion.

entries.title: Dictation runs for up to fifteen minutes
entries.body: Dictation in any text box can run for up to fifteen minutes, longer than before, with a countdown and a warning chime in its last minute and another chime when it stops. Pressing Stop just as it reaches the limit no longer starts a new recording. The Feedback box takes up to 12,000 characters, enough for a long dictated report.

entries.title: Easier to use on a phone or keyboard
entries.body: On a phone or narrow window, the Metadata and profile pages show their search box and a Contents button rather than hiding them. Keyboard focus outlines that were almost invisible in the light theme are drawn in a strong colour. The Search panel's ordering buttons are easier to tap, and text boxes no longer make an iPhone zoom in.

entries.title: Stop and long imports behave predictably
entries.body: Stop on an import behaves consistently: if the last piece of work still produces something usable, that is kept and the article published, and no new paid work starts. Work that overruns its time pauses and retries while retries remain, rather than failing the import, though finishing is not guaranteed. Stopping Illustrated part-way keeps the previous painting.

entries.title: Run-again buttons wait for the new result
entries.body: After you ask a mode to run again (Paint again, Find more and the like), the button stays unavailable until the new result has loaded, so pressing twice quickly no longer starts a second paid run. A mode's Generate button no longer disappears when loading fails, and Skim no longer says your purpose was not saved when it was.

entries.title: Referee no longer deletes your oldest criteria
entries.body: Referee used to delete the oldest finished criterion, without warning, once an article had more than 20. Nothing is deleted now: an article holds up to 200, and past that you are told how many to remove, with your new criterion kept through a reload. Deleting one that has comments is refused in plain words, not with an error.

entries.title: Plainer errors, and fixes for typing and comments
entries.body: Failures that showed a browser error, such as 'Load failed', give a plain sentence. Pressing Enter or Escape to pick a word while typing Japanese or Chinese no longer sends, saves or closes the box. A comment edited while the AI's answer to it appears no longer reverts, and passages found in your library match a chosen topic or tag.
